title: Rosalind and the Bell
premise: When Hazel Ravensworth's twin sister Rosalind dies, Hazel returns to the family house in Hollow Creek to bury her—and finds 'Rosalind' already waiting on the porch, unchanged since 1974, insisting she never left. The thing wearing her sister's face is the childhood imaginary friend made real by an old bargain: in exchange for one twin being spared, the other was promised to the house. As the last living signatory of the 1974 covenant prepares to sell the property to developers, the entity grows desperate and the town's buried disappearances surface. Hazel must uncover what their grandmother took—a child stolen from a neighboring family—and return it, body and name, before the papers are signed, choosing at last to be seen rather than survive unseen.
about_author: Vesper Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales in rural New England, where she learned that every house keeps better records than its family. She writes horror about inheritance, small towns, and the debts that outlive their debtors.

chapters.title: The Wrong Twin
chapters.summary: Hazel arrives in Hollow Creek with an urn and a rental agreement, dreading the funeral of a sister they barely knew. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into dread when the funeral director calls them 'Rosalind' without correction.

chapters.title: Counted Doors
chapters.summary: Hazel settles into the decaying house, counting doors and checking locks as they always have. A child's chalk hopscotch grid appears on the porch overnight. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the comfort of ritual curdling as the house begins responding to them.

chapters.title: She Never Left
chapters.summary: On the porch sits Rosalind—eight years old, sun-faded dress, exactly as Hazel drew her in 1974. She says she waited. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: terror braided with a shameful, aching joy at seeing the friend again.

chapters.title: What the Neighbors Remember
chapters.summary: Hazel visits elderly neighbor Maud Pell, who goes white at the mention of 1974 and warns Hazel not to answer if it knocks twice. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: first confirmation that others know something and chose silence.

chapters.title: The Covenant Papers
chapters.summary: In the attic, Hazel finds a deed addendum dated June 1974, signed by their grandmother, binding 'one child of this house' to the property in perpetuity. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: cold understanding that the imaginary friend was collateral.

chapters.title: Two of Everything
chapters.summary: Rosalind follows Hazel through the house, mimicking childhood games, growing sharper and more present each day. Hazel catches themselves setting two plates. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the seduction of belonging to something, even something wrong.

chapters.title: The Last Signatory
chapters.summary: Hazel tracks down the surviving party to the covenant: developer's lawyer Corinne Ashe, granddaughter of the family whose daughter vanished in 1974. POV: Corinne. Emotional beat: her pragmatic eagerness to close the sale shadowed by a family grief she never examined.

chapters.title: Knock Twice
chapters.summary: Something knocks twice at Maud's door; Maud dies peacefully in her sleep the same night, smiling. Hazel realizes the entity is clearing witnesses. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: grief for Maud fused with the horror of being next.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Version
chapters.summary: The child-Rosalind tells Hazel her side: she saved Hazel from drowning in 1974, and the house only asked for 'a Ravensworth.' POV: alternating Hazel and the entity. Emotional beat: sympathy for the thing, and the first hint it may be a victim too.

chapters.title: The Missing Girl
chapters.summary: Corinne shares her family's sealed records: her aunt Lily disappeared the same week the Ravensworths' well was capped. The dates align perfectly. POV: Corinne. Emotional beat: righteous anger turning toward the house on the hill.

chapters.title: Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Following the entity's own riddling hints, Hazel pries up the old nursery floor and finds a child's shoe, a hair ribbon, and a name scratched into a joist: LILY ASHE. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: nausea—their inheritance is a crime scene.

chapters.title: The House Wakes
chapters.summary: Doors multiply; hallways lengthen; every room contains a memory of Hazel and Rosalind playing. The house wants Hazel to stay and stop asking questions. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: claustrophobic realization that invisibility was always the trap.

chapters.title: Papers on the Table
chapters.summary: Corinne schedules the closing for Friday. That night, her office fills with the smell of pond water and a second set of fingerprints appears on her contracts. POV: Corinne. Emotional beat: professional composure cracking into genuine fear.

chapters.title: The Drowned Hour
chapters.summary: Hazel relives 1974 through the house itself: the pond, the bargain struck by a desperate grandmother, and the truth that both twins were offered—and the house kept Lily instead. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: shattered identity; their whole life was built on someone else's erasure.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Hazel confronts the entity: it isn't Rosalind, it's Lily, wearing the shape Hazel gave her because no one ever gave her a grave or a name. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: compassion replacing fear; justice requires witness, not exorcism.

chapters.title: Corinne Comes Home
chapters.summary: Hazel tells Corinne everything, expecting disbelief; instead Corinne reveals she has dreamed of the porch her whole life. They form an uneasy alliance. POV: Corinne. Emotional beat: two strangers finding belonging in shared inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Delay the Signing
chapters.summary: They stall the closing while digging for Lily's remains, but the developer's crew arrives early and the entity begins taking the workers one by one. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: escalating stakes as outside attention makes concealment impossible.

chapters.title: The Well Opens
chapters.summary: Hazel unseals the capped well and finds Lily below, preserved impossibly, holding the original covenant in her small hands. The house screams through every wall. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: grim triumph shadowed by the knowledge that returning her will cost something.

chapters.title: A Name and a Grave
chapters.summary: On what would have been the closing date, Hazel and Corinne hold a funeral for Lily Ashe, speaking her name aloud before the assembled town. The entity stands among the mourners, finally seen. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: catharsis—justice rendered outside any law, through remembrance.

chapters.title: The House Refuses
chapters.summary: The house, cheated of its Ravensworth, tries to keep Hazel by sealing every exit and offering them Rosalind forever. Hazel must walk out past every version of the friend they ever loved. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the climax of self-erasure versus selfhood.

chapters.title: Signing Away
chapters.summary: Corinne signs the sale with a new clause: the land is deeded to Lily Ashe's memory, untouchable, unbuilt upon. The house exhales, dims, and lets them go. POV: Corinne. Emotional beat: release; paperwork becomes an act of grace.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Hazel stays in Hollow Creek, keeping the empty house's lights on—not as a prisoner but as a keeper. On the porch some evenings, a girl waves, and Hazel waves back. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; belonging chosen freely at last.
